32_marg1501: All wisdom, etc. Jerome says that he found the book of Jesus the son of Sirach among the Hebrews, entitled not Ecclesiasticus, as among the Latins, but Parables; and with it were joined Ecclesiastes and the Song of Songs, so that it matched Solomon not only in the number of books but in the kind of their matter. But the book of Wisdom he did not find among them; rather it smacks of Greek eloquence, and some affirm that it is Philo’s. Ecclesiasticus, like Ecclesiastes, is most useful to the Church; the name means one who gathers or collects, as the other means a preacher. But Ecclesiastes is referred to Christ, Ecclesiasticus to any preacher, who for the excellence of his virtues is called Panaretos, that is, capable of all the virtues. Its clearness and its Latinity are so great that it is its own commentary.
32_marg1502: All wisdom, etc. Rabanus. He begins from the eternal wisdom of God, which is Christ, who is always with the Father before the ages, according to that: “In the beginning was the Word: and the Word was with God,” etc.
32_marg1503: From the Lord God, etc. Because Christ, the fountain of life, the true light, is born of the Father, and “all things were made by him: and without him was made nothing”, whoever lacks this wisdom “walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth”. For “the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God”, and “the wisdom of the flesh is death”.
32_marg1504: Who hath numbered the sand of the sea, etc. Rabanus. He compares bodily things with spiritual, so that what is wholly impossible may be judged from what is most difficult. For if no one can number these things, which were made in fixed number and measure and weight, how much less can he search out the wisdom of God, without beginning and without end, unutterable, beyond reckoning.
32_marg1505: Created according to his manhood: that is, in the counsel of God the Father he was foreordained to be incarnate for the salvation of the human race. Note that, because of the unity of the person, Christ is sometimes said to be begotten, sometimes created.
32_marg1506: The origin of all wisdom proceeds from the Word of God, which as God abides always with the Father in heaven; but, entering the world by the dispensation of his manhood, he gave the commandments of salvation. Whence: “Thou hast the words of eternal life.”
32_marg1507: He shows that no one can fathom the depth of God, or the greatness of his goodness and mercy. Hence, for the freeing and enlightening of the human race, he deigned to become man. Whence: “who shall declare his generation?”
32_marg1508: He created her, etc. That is, through the Word coeternal with him, together with the Holy Spirit, he ordered the coming of the Only-begotten: how, through the Virgin’s childbearing, he would come for the salvation of the world, restore creation, and call man back to the knowledge and love of himself, giving him the gift of the Holy Spirit, that by his gift he may be saved for ever.
32_interl4027: in the present, of right confession
32_marg1509: The fear of the Lord, etc. “Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord: he shall delight exceedingly in his commandments. … Glory and wealth shall be in his house,” etc.
32_marg1510: The fear of the Lord is honour, etc. Rabanus. There are two kinds of fear. Of the one it is said: “Fear is not in charity,” etc. Those who have it stop sinning for fear of hell and amend their life; this fear brings in charity, but is cast out. For he who fears in this way does not yet love or desire good things, but shuns evil ones; yet he amends himself and begins to desire good things. Of the other it is written: “The fear of the Lord is holy, enduring for ever and ever.” For each one fears lest he lose good things and the presence of God, which he desires to enjoy for ever; of which it is said: The fear of the Lord shall delight the heart. This gives inward sweetness here, and eternal life in the future.
32_interl4034: at the end of this life
32_interl4037: at the end of this life
32_marg1511: The love of God, etc. Rabanus. The love of God is the true wisdom, which “is poured forth in our hearts, by the Holy Ghost”, who fills us with the sweetness of the love of God in the knowledge of his great works. Whence: “you have the unction from the Holy One, and know all things,” etc. For the spiritual unction is the Spirit himself, whose sacrament is in the visible anointing; his grace teaches us of all things. Otherwise the teacher’s words are idle. But the love of God, which is the gift of the Spirit, makes us understand and keep the commandments of God most quickly. For it begins the good and perfects it; it will be the reward in the future. Whence: “thou shalt fill me with joy with thy countenance: at thy right hand are delights even to the end.”

32_marg1512: The fear of the Lord, etc. Without the fear of God and the keeping of his commandments there is no religion. Whence: “if any man think himself to be religious, not bridling his tongue, but deceiving his own heart, this man’s religion is vain,” etc.
32_marg1513: Him, namely, who by the fear of God keeps the rule of justice in faith, teaching and deed.

32_marg1515: Through the divine wisdom man has the knowledge to shun evil and the understanding to do good; for in the end it works both in the hearer. Whence: “He that hearkeneth to me, shall not be confounded: and they that work by me, shall not sin. They that explain me shall have life everlasting.” “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. A good understanding to all that do it.”
32_marg1516: In the treasures, etc. In meditation on the law both are made plain: how evils are to be shunned, and how spiritual wisdom is to be learned and good works practised, in which true religion lies.
32_marg1517: Wisdom, etc. Which forbids sins and fleshly desires. Whence: “A corrupt man loveth not one that reproveth him: nor will he go to the wise.”
32_marg1518: The fear of the Lord, etc. Because through penance it cleanses from past sins, or holds back from committing them.
32_marg1519: Because he who does not amend himself through the fear of God falls into the whirlpool of sin.

32_marg1520: A good understanding, etc. Hence in Proverbs: “the lips of the wise preserve them.” And elsewhere: “The prudent man doth all things with counsel: but he that is a fool, layeth open his folly.” So it is the part of a wise man to hold his words and do all things with moderation.
32_marg1521: Shall declare, etc. Even-mindedly, rendering not evil for evil, but good for good.
32_marg1522: Son, if thou desire, etc. Wisdom herself shows how you may come to wisdom: for without keeping justice no one comes to the summit of wisdom. Whence James: “Who is a wise man, and endued with knowledge among you? Let him shew, by a good conversation, his work in the meekness of wisdom.”
32_marg1523: For … wisdom, etc. As has often been said, the fear of the Lord is the keeping of wisdom and discipline; to it belong right faith and temperance of conduct, because “without faith it is impossible to please God”, and the life of the good is always peaceful. Whence: “Learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart: and you shall find rest to your souls.” For he who truly fears God cannot be without faith and good works, which fill a man with virtues and make him acceptable to God. Whence: “To a man that is good in his sight, God hath given wisdom, and knowledge … but to the sinner he hath given vexation, and superfluous care.”
32_interl4060: elsewhere: be not stubborn and incredulous to the fear of God
32_interl4061: “he that cometh to God, must believe that he is, and is a rewarder to them that seek him”
32_interl4062: He who seeks God in simplicity finds him. Whence: “The simplicity of the just shall guide them: and the deceitfulness of the wicked shall destroy them.”
32_marg1524: “A double minded man is inconstant in all his ways”: he, namely, who wants to rejoice with the world and reign with Christ.
32_interl4063: like those who with a wicked heart devise evil and at all times sow discord
32_marg1525: Bearing one thing in the heart and showing another in deed. Whence: “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in the clothing of sheep,” etc.
32_marg1526: Watch over them, etc. It is plain that he who follows heretics earns damnation for his soul, because in the judgement the secrets of hearts will be revealed and to each will be rendered according to his works; for God will destroy “all that speak a lie”, he who abhors “the bloody and the deceitful man”. Whence: “Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.” And elsewhere: “The lord of that servant shall come … and shall separate him, and appoint his portion with the hypocrites. There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”
32_marg1527: Son, when thou comest, etc. Rabanus. He has shown what is to be shunned; now he shows what is to be done, saying: Son, when thou comest to the service of God, stand in justice, etc. For he who wishes to keep himself from the allurements of the world and “live godly in Christ” suffers persecution. For while he makes ready to gird himself for the divine service, he stirs up the devil’s war against himself; and while he subdues some vices he struggles against others; and it is brought about by divine ordering that he both conquers and is conquered, lest he be lifted up. But because humility and patience are necessary to him, there follows: Humble thy heart, and endure, etc.
32_interl4066: because no one knows how to do this unless he is instructed by the divine commandments

32_interl4071: as if: in the time of affliction be long-suffering and brave; “do manfully, and let thy heart take courage”
32_marg1528: Keep patience, etc. “In your patience you shall possess your souls”; because, namely, patience is the root and guardian of all the virtues. But it should be known that patience is exercised in three ways. We are scourged by God, and must beware not to murmur; we bear persecutions, losses and insults from our neighbour, and must beware not to render evil for evil; we are tempted by the adversary, and must take care not to be bent to the delight of sin or to consent, nor to seek present things in return for these, but to wait for the things to come.
32_marg1529: Believe God, etc. The afflicted man must believe, and direct the steps of his works in the sight of God, and hope in him. Whence: “Commit thy way to the Lord, and trust in him, and he will do it.” Hence Jeremias says: “Blessed be the man that trusteth in the Lord, and the Lord shall be his confidence,” etc.
32_marg1530: Ye that fear the Lord, etc. “The Lord taketh pleasure in them that fear him: and in them that hope in his mercy.” For he who truly fears waits patiently for his mercy. But “they that depart from thee, shall be written in the earth”, and confounded.
32_marg1531: Ye that fear the Lord, believe him, etc. He urges those who fear the Lord to believe him, because they will come to a sure reward. “For the just man liveth by faith.” Whence: “Be of good heart, son, thy sins are forgiven thee.” And elsewhere: “thy faith hath made thee whole.”
32_marg1532: Ye that fear the Lord, hope in him, etc. He commends three things to those who fear God: to believe, to hope, to love; because by faith, hope and charity God is truly worshipped and one comes to contemplation, which is eternal blessedness.
32_marg1533: My children behold, etc. Rabanus. Here too he says three things: that no one who hopes in the Lord is confounded, nor one who abides in his commandments forsaken, nor one who calls on him despised; because “with the heart, we believe unto justice; but, with the mouth, confession is made unto salvation”, and “he that doth the will of my Father … shall enter into the kingdom of heaven”. And he says well that in the time of tribulation sins are forgiven to all who seek God in truth, because “a sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit,” etc. And “the Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him: to all that call upon him in truth”.
32_marg1534: Woe to them that are of a double heart and to … lips, etc. He warned that no one should come to God with a double heart; now he says: Woe to them that are of a double heart, etc. For he who thinks and speaks wicked things and persists in wicked works will perish for ever unless he repents.
32_marg1535: He goes on the earth two ways who does evil and hopes for good; or who follows the works of the flesh and thinks he is perfecting the sanctification of the spirit in fear; or who shows in deed what is God’s and seeks in thought what is the world’s. Such men are “inconstant in all their ways”, because they are easily frightened in adversity and ensnared in prosperity.
32_marg1536: That are fainthearted, etc. Still he teaches to shun error and to love virtue. For he who desires God’s protection must keep a sincere faith and have constancy of mind. For he who doubts in faith and wavers in hope does not come to the crown of life, which yet is promised to those who truly fear, who, namely, “bring forth fruit in patience”. But those who in the judgement, namely by apostasy or heresy, depart from the faith and persist in wicked works will be tormented for ever. Whence: to “them that … obey not the truth, but give credit to iniquity, wrath and indignation,” etc.
32_marg1537: Shall begin to examine, etc. Though God examines all things at all times, he is said to examine when he is seen to approve or disapprove something.
32_marg1538: They that fear the Lord, will not be incredulous, etc. He treats by turns of the love, the fear and the love of God, because “the fear of the Lord … endureth for ever and ever”, and “every one that loveth, is born of God, and knoweth God”. He, then, who fears and loves God believes the Scriptures, keeps the commandments of God by doing them, and by constant meditation seeks what is well pleasing to him. So he will be filled with wisdom and with the love of God. For “the end of the commandment is charity”, and “he that loveth his neighbour, hath fulfilled the law”.
32_marg1539: They that fear the Lord, will prepare, etc. Happy the soul that daily cleanses its heart to receive God as its dweller; he who possesses him lacks no good, because he has in himself the author of all good things. And because for this are needed the keeping of the commandments and patience in good work, by which one comes to the knowledge of the truth, there follows: They that fear the Lord, keep his Commandments, etc.
32_marg1540: “The just is first accuser of himself.” For as a reward awaits humility, so punishment awaits pride. Whence John: “If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves.”
32_marg1541: He who is truly wise is a true worshipper of justice, because wisdom lays down the rule of justice.
32_interl4079: “according to the height of the heaven above the earth: he hath strengthened his mercy towards them that fear him,” etc.
32_interl4080: obedience and love are the virtues of the just, but figuratively by the virtues he means the possessor of the virtues
32_marg1542: The judgment of the father: of God, “of whom all paternity in heaven and earth is named”, because all things are from him. He loves what he has made, and that it should abide in him by whom it was made; he who hears his judgement and does his commandments will be saved. His commandment is that reverence be shown also to one’s earthly father and mother. Whence: “Honour thy father,” etc. Whence there follows: For God hath made … honourable. One to whom God has given honour must not be dishonoured by his children, because God by his judgement will search out how his commandment is kept.
32_marg1543: He, namely, who keeps the commandments and abstains from sins, and yet does not cease to pray for his transgressions, because he knows that the merciful Judge hears prayers at all times.
32_marg1544: To honour one’s parents is “the first commandment with a promise”.
32_marg1545: In his offspring, or in his disciples, in whose upbringing those rejoice who obey their masters or parents; or better, they receive as children the fruit of good works.
32_marg1546: “He that turneth away his ears from hearing the law, his prayer shall be an abomination.” But he who obeys the commandments of God, his prayer will be directed “as incense”.
32_marg1547: Not, namely, in the womb; whence it is shown that the spiritual father is most worthy of honour. Whence Paul: “by the gospel I have begotten you.” And elsewhere: “Let the priests that rule well, be esteemed worthy of double honour: especially they who labour in the word and doctrine.”
32_marg1548: The father’s blessing, etc. Rabanus. The patriarchs blessed their sons: as Noah blessed Sem and Japheth, and cursed the posterity of Cham. Abraham too gave a blessing to his son Isaac, Isaac to Jacob, and Jacob to the twelve patriarchs; in them was prefigured he who descended from the stock of the patriarchs, “who is over all things, God blessed for ever”. And how the curse of parents harms their offspring was shown in the seed of Cham, which was blotted out of the land of promise by the sons of Sem, that is, the Israelites.
32_marg1549: Cham mocked his father’s nakedness and condemned his seed to perpetual slavery. Absalom too drove David from the kingdom and defiled his concubines, but paid fitting penalties by his death. The boys of Bethel mocked Eliseus’ baldness, and two bears out of the forest tore forty-two of them; because the childish folly of the Jews mocked Christ crucified in the place of Calvary, but in the forty-second year after his ascension two bears, that is, Vespasian and Titus, came out of the forest of the Gentiles and tore the mockers most savagely.
32_interl4085: children after the flesh, or disciples, ought to cherish their parents with honour and comfort, that the affection of charity may so grow; whence: let them “make a return of duty to their parents: for this is acceptable before God”
32_marg1550: Alms, namely, which blots out sin. For the victim which is offered “for sin” is called sin; but he who has pity on his parents or on other poor people will receive the reward of justice, freed from his sins.
32_marg1551: “Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.” And elsewhere: “He that hath mercy on the poor, lendeth to the Lord.”
32_marg1552: Hence Daniel to Nabuchodonosor: “Wherefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable to thee, and redeem thou thy sins with alms, and thy iniquities with works of mercy to the poor: perhaps he will forgive thy offences.” Hence the Lord says: “give alms; and behold, all things are clean unto you.”
32_interl4087: he is wicked and infamous who neglects his parents
32_marg1553: Meekness and humility bring forth grace, pride and fury ruin. Whence: “Learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart: and you shall find rest to your souls.” And elsewhere: “whosoever shall exalt himself, shall be humbled,” etc.
32_marg1554: The greater thou art, etc. Above he taught meekness of conduct and humility of works; now he teaches purity of heart, lest human reason heedlessly discuss what it cannot comprehend. Whence Ecclesiastes: “Speak not any thing rashly, and let not thy heart be hasty to utter a word before God,” etc. Hence Paul says: “not to be more wise than it behoveth to be wise,” etc. It is enough for a man to think devoutly on the things God has commanded and to fulfil them in deed.
32_marg1555: In unnecessary matters, etc. That is, do not search needlessly into what you cannot know by reasoning. Whence Ecclesiastes: “What needeth a man to seek things that are above him?” etc. A sober understanding is best in all things; it refreshes the soul and does not weigh down the mind. Whence: “Thou hast found honey, eat what is sufficient for thee, lest being glutted therewith thou vomit it”, and forswear the name of thy God.
32_marg1556: Heretics come about in two ways: by disputing beyond measure either about the Creator or about the creature they fall into errors and depart from the truth.
32_marg1557: Because “according to thy hardness … thou treasurest up to thyself wrath, against the day of wrath”.

32_marg1558: A heart that goeth, etc. Because it does not take care or strive to avoid, and because it loves, the things that lead to destruction, such as heresies and profane novelties. Whence there follows: A heart that goeth two ways, etc.

32_interl4104: as water quenches fire, so alms poured out through charity smothers the flame of sin; whence: “when thou dost alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doth”
32_marg1559: Son, defraud not the poor of alms, etc. God shows how much alms avails, saying: “give alms; and behold, all things are clean unto you.” And to those who will be on his right he will say: “Come, ye blessed of my Father, possess you the kingdom prepared for you … For I was hungry, and you gave me to eat,” etc. But there are many kinds of alms; for not only he who gives necessities to the needy, but also he who grants pardon for a sin gives alms, and he who from his heart rebukes in words or deeds.
32_marg1560: Afflict not the heart of the needy, etc. Alms is not to be put off when there is the means of giving. Whence: “Say not to thy friend: Go, and come again … when thou canst give at present.” And elsewhere: “He that despiseth his neighbour, sinneth: but he that sheweth mercy to the poor, shall be blessed.” But alms is to be given “not with sadness, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver”. Hence the poor widow “cast in more than all” into the treasury, because God weighs not the size of the gift but the devotion of the heart.
32_marg1561: Turn not away … from the poor, etc. The poor man is not to be provoked by anger but soothed with gentle speech. For “the anger of man worketh not the justice of God”, and “he that stoppeth his ear against the cry of the poor, shall also cry himself and shall not be heard”. For he who can give ought to, because “a secret present quencheth anger, and a gift in the bosom the greatest wrath”. But for him who cannot, “a good word is better than the best gift”. “He that hath the substance of this world, and shall see his brother in need, and shall shut up his bowels from him: how doth the charity of God abide in him?” For “faith … if it have not works, is dead”. So let us not love “in word, nor in tongue, but in deed, and in truth”.
32_marg1562: In these are commended meekness and humility; for meekness spurns no one, humility subjects itself to all. It becomes a Christian to be affable and mild to his equals and inferiors, humble to his elders. Whence: “Lord, my heart is not exalted: nor are my eyes lofty,” etc.

32_marg1563: Deliver him that suffereth wrong, etc. As he said that giving to the poor is alms, so he shows that freeing one unjustly oppressed is mercy. Whence: “Deliver them that are led to death.”
32_marg1564: He leaves out no kind of alms: to the poor and to parents he adds orphans and widows, that we may bring them help. For as a father’s affection is to be given to the orphan, so the comfort of a husband to the widow.

For whoever keeps the precepts of wisdom is wary in the changing of the times, nor does he forsake the way of justice in the time of persecution and distress. 32_marg1570: Hide not thy wisdom, etc. Wisdom is not to be hidden from those who wish to hear. For “he that hideth up corn, shall be cursed among the people: but a blessing upon the head of them that sell”. Whence: “Trade till I come.”

32_marg1571: In nowise speak against the truth, etc. One must obey one’s elders if they agree with truth and justice, and not otherwise; but for the right faith and true religion, in which lies the soul’s salvation, one must contend. 32_interl4151: that is, do not consent to him who entices thee to sin
32_interl4152: adversaries are overcome not by human strength but by divine help; whence: “I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to resist”
32_marg1572: Be not hasty, etc. “Death and life are in the power of the tongue.” “He that keepeth his mouth and his tongue, keepeth his soul from distress.” “He that hath no guard on his speech shall meet with evils.” Hence James says: “let every man be swift to hear, but slow to speak, and slow to anger.” Hence elsewhere it is written: “the kingdom of God is not in speech, but in power.”

32_marg1573: In the Church the heretics are like lions, who by the glibness of their tongue lead astray the hearts of the innocent and by the insolence of their conduct disturb the meekness of the simple.

The third, that he put all he thinks useful and necessary after the good of charity and peace. The fourth, that he wholly cease from anger. The fifth, that he desire to heal his brother’s anger, even if unreasonable, because another’s sadness is as ruinous as one’s own unless, so far as lies in you, you drive it from your brother’s mind as well. 32_marg1636: The Lord hath overthrown the lands of the Gentiles, etc. When he cast Jerusalem down to its foundations by the Romans, burned the temple, and destroyed the transgressors. These words can also be referred to the persecutors of the Christians and the martyrs of Christ. For the princes of the world who persecuted the Church of Christ perished by a wondrous death, and afterwards their posterity was blotted out and the glory of the martyrs exalted. Whence: “The Lord keepeth all them that love him; but all the wicked he will destroy.”
32_marg1637: Pride was not made for men, etc. The vices were not created in men but found out by a perverse will; for God made all things very good. But “the beginning of the pride of man, is to fall off from God”.
32_marg1638: As if: through the softness of mind which the female sex denotes, wrath rises up, which the constancy of virtue overcomes.
32_marg1639: Holy teachers are held in honour among the good, especially those who fear the Lord. Whence: “Let the priests that rule well, be esteemed worthy of double honour,” etc.

32_marg1640: Truly it is glory to fear God. For he who fears keeps justice in all things. Whence: “have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ … with respect of persons.”
32_marg1641: The great man, and the judge, etc. Though earthly power is a great thing, it cannot surpass one who fears the Lord; for “there is no want to them that fear him”, but “the rich have wanted, and have suffered hunger,” etc.

32_marg1642: They that are free shall serve a servant that is wise, etc. Literally, it often happens that a man of low birth, through the nobility of knowledge and faith, is set before the nobly born. Whence: “A wise servant shall rule over foolish sons.” Mystically, the servant of the Church, who devoutly keeps the Christian religion, is set before the synagogue. Whence: “The elder shall serve the younger”, and “Jacob I have loved, but Esau I have hated.”
